newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-DOLPHINS EXTEND MARINO'S CONTRACT, SIGN TOP PICK GREEN.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-DOLPHINS EXTEND MARINO'S CONTRACT, SIGN TOP PICK GREEN.

text.p: The Hall of Fame will have to wait a little longer for Dan Marino after the record-setting quarterback signed a contract extention to play for the Miami Dolphins through the 1999 season.
Marino, the NFL's all-time leader in pass attempts, completions, passing yardage and touchdown passes, had signed a three-year deal in April 1996 but agreed to another year on Friday.
"I signed the extension to help the Dolphins make more room under the salary cap," said the 35-year-old Marino, who has played his entire career with the Dolphins.
"I'm happy to help the club out in this way," added Marino, who completed 221 of 373 passes in 1996 for 2,795 yards with 17 touchdowns and nine interceptions in just 13 games.
"With the players we have coming back, along with our new acquisitions, I think we'll have a very good team this year."

One of those new acquisitions is first-round draft pick, wide receiver Yatil Green, who signed a five-year contract Friday. Green was the 15th overall selection in the NFL draft out of the University of Miami.

"I'm happy that we were able to get Yatil signed as quickly as we did," said Dolphins general manager/head coach Jimmy Johnson. "I believe that Yatil will be a big part of the success that we hope to achieve this year."
In his junior year at Miami, Green caught 42 passes for 669 yards and three touchdowns for college career totals of 82 receptions for 1,397 yards and nine TDs.
